methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Recognition that Virginia's AI challenge centers on small-business adoption reveals the gap between concentrated data center infrastructure investment and distributed economic capability—signals shallow penetration outside tech hubs despite physical AI infrastructure presence.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab delivering hands-on professional training represents distributed deep-learning infrastructure in a non-metro region, potentially seeding peer-to-peer AI fluency networks beyond the NoVA-Richmond corridor.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target the technology gap through grassroots skill-building, signaling distributed capability development through accessible training rather than platform dependency or concentrated excellence.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership concentrates advanced AI education and innovation capacity in Richmond's academic-nonprofit ecosystem, deepening metro capability but raising questions about regional knowledge diffusion mechanisms to surrounding areas.

signals.title: Press Release: Morgan Griffith Announces HHS Grant to Virginia Tech for AI Health Care Research - Quiver Quantitative
signals.signal_reading: Federal HHS grant to Virginia Tech for AI healthcare research reinforces New River Valley as a specialized AI research node, but grant-dependent academic work often stays concentrated within university networks rather than distributing to regional small businesses and practitioners.
